tolerance.comparison_method: Open CASCADE re-import; compare axis-aligned bounding box, solid count, and volume. Normative standard dimensions are the primary acceptance criterion; vendor STEP files are secondary geometric oracles.

external_references.notes: Head diameter and overall length match ISO 4762 within 0.01 mm. The parametric detailed screw is one closed solid whose blind hex socket is bounded by a 45-degree conical countersink and a 70-degree conical drill point, each trimmed by the six flats; its volume is 128.131 mm3 against the golden's 128.119 (0.01%). Surface entities match the reference inventory (plane 9, cone 5, cylinder 2); the reference writes one rim-cone face and this generator writes six patches of the same cone entity, so the advanced-face count is 21 against 16.

Head diameter and overall length match ISO 4762 within 0.01 mm. The golden socket is at the nominal across-flats (below the ISO minimum); the parametric part uses the ISO upper limit s_max, so the sockets intentionally differ.

The reference head diameter is 9.2003 mm, which exceeds the ISO 4762:2004 maximum dk = 8.5 mm for M5. The overall length matches, but the model is not a conforming ISO 4762 M5 reference and is not used as a normative oracle.

Shielded 608ZZ: one solid with a recessed 45-degree shield groove on each face and no rolling elements. The parametric shielded envelope matches the golden's solid count, surface classes, vertex rings, and volume.

parametric_value.note: Exact B-slot6 section with analytic corner and bore arcs

external_references.notes: The 20 x 20 x 50 envelope matches, and the dedicated b_slot6_2020_extrusion builder reproduces the manufacturer-specific section: 174.3364 mm^2, 12 cylindrical faces at radii 1.0 and 2.75 mm, and zero bidirectional surface deviation. The reference splits each end cap into four coplanar faces (96 plane entities); the parametric model has two cap faces (86 plane entities).

external_references.standard: catalog record: module 2.0, 20 teeth, width 16, bore 8
external_references.notes: The reference is a blank tip-diameter envelope. The parametric envelope matches it exactly: tip diameter 44 mm, face width 16 mm, bore 8 mm, and volume 23524.2 mm3. No tooth form is claimed for this reference.

Detailed reference: nominal-diameter shank, a 45-degree countersink with a 22.5-degree conical top-edge break (0.05 mm inset), and a conical socket (45-degree rim over a hexagon at the nominal 2.0 mm across flats, 70-degree drill point). The reference socket reaches the head underside at the hex corners and its drill point enters the shank, deeper than ISO 10642's nominal t = 1.2 mm; the deeper reference socket is modeled and recorded. Volume 96.478 vs 96.488 mm3 (0.01%).

Detailed nut: a true conical washer face on each bearing face (60 degrees) trimmed by the six flats, plus the reference bore lead-in. The across-flats is checked from the face-circle vertex ring, because OCCT's Bnd_Box includes the untrimmed conical surfaces and cannot confirm s. The golden M5 uses the old DIN 934 height 4.0 mm against ISO 4032's 4.7 mm; the standard value is modeled.
DIN 125 A M3 dimensions (d1 3.2, d2 7, h 0.5) match the golden and ISO 7089; the golden is a standard-correct plain washer.

DIN 125 A M8: d1 8.4, d2 16, h nominal 1.6 mm (limits 1.4..1.8). The reference is 1.8 mm, the ISO 7089 h_max, so the reference thickness is chosen at h_max to reproduce the golden within the standard.

DIN 127 B M4: d1 4.1, d2 7.6, s 0.9, h 1.8. The downloaded reference has four B-spline side surfaces and two planar caps (6 faces, 12 edges, 8 vertices) and a parallel-plane split at the +X side. The parametric part uses the same native topology and reproduces the reference's eight split-cap vertices exactly (corner endpoint overrides from the reference), with smooth cubic B-spline sides. Volume 27.43 vs 27.64 mm3; exact tessellated bbox 7.603 x 7.636 x 1.751 mm. The golden's exact bbox is 7.592 x 7.600 x 1.751 mm; OCCT Bnd_Box reports the looser 9.915 x 11.120 x 1.773 mm control hull for the golden's high-degree surfaces. DIN side length b = 1.5; the radial section width is (d2 - d1) / 2 = 1.75 mm.

bbox_axes.label: outer diameter across the split gap

external_references.notes: DIN 440 V M5: d2 18, square hole 5.5, s 2.0. The golden and parametric part both have one analytic outer cylinder, four planar square-hole walls, and two planar end faces (7 faces, 15 edges, 10 vertices); volume and area match to rounding.
DIN 7349 M3: d1 3.2, d2 9, s 1.0. The golden and parametric part are the same analytic annular solid of revolution (two cylinders, two planes); bbox, area, and volume match to rounding.

external_references.family: hexagon socket set screw with flat point
external_references.notes: DIN 913 M3 x 5: d 3, socket s 1.5 (upper limit 1.545), socket depth t 2.0, 90-degree point cone; the downloaded reference uses a 2.2 mm point flat, so the parametric part matches that reference value (DIN d_p max is 2.0), which places the cone end at z = 0.4 and makes the Z=0..1 cross-sections coincide. The reference's socket across flats 1.5588 is above the DIN max 1.545, so the socket uses the standard limit; that accounts for the remaining volume difference (30.522 vs 30.447 mm3). Both have the same 11-face topology (1 cylinder, 1 cone, 9 planes; 23 edges, 15 vertices).

DIN 93 M4: d1 4.3, d2 14, tab 5 wide x 14 long, s 0.38. The tab transition center is l/2 + 2 = 9 mm and the tangent fillet radius is 4.25 mm, matching the reference. Both parts have one outer cylinder, two transition cylinders, one bore cylinder, two tab-side planes, a tab-end plane, and two caps (9 faces, 21 edges, 14 vertices); volume and area match to rounding.

Head diameter 7.6 mm and overall length 12.2 mm (= 10 + k 2.2) match ISO 7380. The parametric head is one closed solid with a spherical dome and a blind hex socket; the conical socket rim and floor are typed omissions, so volume is not compared. The golden socket and dome are at the ISO upper limits (s_max, r_f max) and the parametric part matches.
Head diameter 9.5 mm and overall length 14.75 mm (= 12 + k 2.75) match ISO 7380. The golden socket and dome are at the ISO upper limits (s_max, r_f max) and the parametric part matches.

The reference sharp head diameter 8.0 (within ISO 7.53-8.96) and k 2.3 are used. Its edge radius 0.1725 is below the ISO minimum 0.2, so the parametric part uses 0.2; its socket across flats 2.60 and depth 1.8 exceed the ISO maxima 2.58 and 1.65, so the parametric part uses the ISO maxima.

The reference head profile (sharp dk 10.0, k 2.8, edge radius 0.21) matches exactly. Its socket across flats 3.10 and depth 2.3 exceed the ISO maxima 3.08 and 2.00; the parametric part uses the ISO maxima.

external_references.standard: catalog record: module 2.0, 40 teeth, width 16, bore 10
external_references.notes: The reference is a blank tip-diameter envelope. The parametric envelope matches it exactly: tip diameter 84 mm, face width 16 mm, bore 10 mm, and volume 87411.7 mm3. No tooth form is claimed for this reference.
Plain analytic annulus: two cylindrical surfaces and two planar faces; the measured volume matches the standard d1/d2/h table exactly.
Plain analytic annulus: two cylindrical surfaces and two planar faces; the measured volume matches the standard d1/d2/h table exactly.
Plain analytic annulus: two cylindrical surfaces and two planar faces; the measured volume matches the standard d1/d2/h table exactly.

Hexagonal body, thickness, and the analytic 1.5 mm bore match the reference; volume is 45.909 mm3. The reference catalog uses the same body for slide-in, drop-in, and hammer styles, so no style-specific retention feature is claimed.
Body dimensions, analytic 2.0 mm bore, and volume match the reference. Slot series is an engagement parameter, not a body feature.
Body dimensions, analytic 2.5 mm bore, and volume match the reference. The M5 body is also used for slot-6 catalog entries.
The revolved profile reproduces the reference's two knurl bands, three plain outer bands, bore, and six annular/planar shoulders; volume and bounding box match exactly.
Same construction as the short insert; knurl bands occupy 20-32% and 68-80% of the length, matching the reference exactly.

Frame, bolt spacing, mounting-hole pattern, shaft diameter, and overall length match. Each of the four mounting holes is one analytic cylindrical surface, matching the reference's per-hole cylinders. The parametric body, pilot boss, and shaft are three separately closed solids because the kernel-free writer does not trim a union; the reference fuses them into one. Volume is 0.63% higher because this builder uses the standard NEMA 22 mm pilot diameter while the reference uses a smaller simplified 17.766 mm boss.

Frame, bolt spacing, mounting-hole pattern, shaft diameter, and overall length match. Each mounting hole is one analytic cylinder. The reference fuses body, boss, and shaft into one solid; this builder layers three watertight solids. Volume is 2.48% higher because the standard 38.1 mm NEMA 23 pilot replaces the reference's simplified 23.688 mm boss.

Bore, outside diameter, length, two outer retaining grooves, and end counterbores are modelled. The reference's intermediate 4.6 mm bore relief is simplified to a 12.4 mm counterbore at each end, so volume is 0.80% low. Rolling elements, cage, seals, and recirculation grooves are omitted in both representations.

external_references.standard: LM-series boundary dimensions with a round flange; envelope only
external_references.notes: Flange diameter, flange thickness, body diameter, length, and bore match exactly; the reference frame is axis X with the flange at -X and the example's orient flag reproduces it.

Legs, thickness, toe radii, and length match; the concave root fillet is sampled with 16 line segments because the kernel's arc-profile path only accepts counter-clockwise minor arcs, so volume is 0.015% high and the reference's analytic root cylinder is replaced by planar facets.
Rectangular blank centered on the XY origin and on z, matching the reference frame; volume and bounding box match exactly. Hole patterns are caller-supplied.
V-Slot wheel body only; the 625 bearings and shims are separate parts. The Xem Studio model is CC BY 4.0. Bounding box, volume, surface counts, and the 45 degree groove cones match.
